title: File system (fs)
lede: Node-fs-shaped file I/O for config, data, and logs. The sync set is the core; the async variants (callback + Promise), the callback file operations and the read/write streams run on a background thread pool and call back from the event loop. readFileSync and readFile return a Buffer of the file's exact bytes without an encoding and a string with one. The file streams and the callback operations are Node's own code ported to TypeScript (Buffer chunks, Node's options, errors as 'error' events).

entries.name: fs.readFileSync(path[, 'utf8'])
entries.signature: readFileSync(path: string | number): Buffer; readFileSync(path: string | number, encoding: BufferEncoding | { encoding: BufferEncoding, flag?: string }): string
entries.description: Reads the whole file: a Buffer of its exact bytes with no encoding, a string with one (a bare encoding or { encoding }), decoded as buf.toString(encoding). A file descriptor reads to its end, so readFileSync(0, 'utf8') is all of stdin. Throws a catchable Error with Node's message, code, syscall and path if the file can't be opened.

params.name: path
params.desc: Path to read, or an open file descriptor (0 is stdin).

params.name: encoding
params.desc: Optional. Any Buffer encoding (utf8, hex, base64, base64url, latin1, ascii, utf16le); a string literal, as the codec is chosen at compile time.

returns.desc: The file's bytes, or its decoded text with an encoding.

differences: With `'utf8'` the string is strlen-based: an embedded null byte truncates it (the Buffer form keeps every byte); a non-`'utf8'` encoding is a clean rejection.

entries.name: fs.writeFileSync(path, data[, opts])
entries.signature: writeFileSync(path: string, data: string | ArrayBuffer | TypedArray, opts?: 'utf8' | { encoding?: 'utf8', flag?: string }): void
entries.description: Creates or truncates the file with data, throwing on failure. data may be a string (the strlen-based path) or an ArrayBuffer/TypedArray (binary-safe, writes the real byte count via fwrite) — dispatched on data's inferred type. The optional third argument accepts 'utf8' / { encoding: 'utf8', flag }; { flag: 'a' } appends instead of truncating, { flag: 'w' } (default) truncates.

params.name: data
params.desc: Content; binary for the typed-array forms.

params.name: opts
params.desc: Optional. encoding only 'utf8'; flag 'a'* appends. mode and other encodings reject.

differences: The options argument supports only `{ encoding: 'utf8', flag, mode }` — a non-`'utf8'` encoding is a clean rejection. `{ mode }` sets the permission bits when the write creates the file (umask-reduced, applied only on creation, matching Node/open(2)).
A file descriptor in place of the path (`fs.writeFileSync(fd, …)`) is a compile error.

entries.name: fs.appendFileSync(path, data[, opts])
entries.signature: appendFileSync(path: string, data: string | ArrayBuffer | TypedArray, opts?: 'utf8' | { encoding?: 'utf8', flag?: string }): void
entries.description: Like writeFileSync, but appends instead of truncating (creates the file if it doesn't exist). Throws on failure. Same string/ArrayBuffer/TypedArray dispatch as writeFileSync. The optional third argument 'utf8' / { encoding: 'utf8', flag } is accepted (the flag is a no-op — it always appends).
differences: The options argument supports only `{ encoding: 'utf8', flag, mode }` — a non-`'utf8'` encoding is a clean rejection. `{ mode }` sets the permission bits when the write creates the file (umask-reduced, applied only on creation, matching Node/open(2)).
A file descriptor in place of the path (`fs.appendFileSync(fd, …)`) is a compile error.

entries.name: fs.existsSync(path)
entries.signature: existsSync(path: string): boolean
entries.description: Plain existence check via POSIX access(). Deliberately does not throw for a missing path — matching real Node's own existsSync, one of the few fs functions that reports "doesn't exist" as false rather than an error.

entries.name: fs.unlinkSync(path)
entries.signature: unlinkSync(path: string): void
entries.description: Deletes a file. Throws on failure.

entries.name: fs.mkdirSync(path)
entries.signature: mkdirSync(path: string): void
entries.description: Creates a directory via POSIX mkdir(), mode 0777 reduced by the process umask as usual.
differences: No `{recursive: true}` option — throws (e.g. `EEXIST`) if the path already exists or a parent directory is missing.

entries.name: fs.rmdirSync(path)
entries.signature: rmdirSync(path: string, options?: { recursive: true }): void
entries.description: Removes an empty directory via POSIX rmdir() — deliberately directory-only (fails on a plain file, unlike unlinkSync). With { recursive: true } it removes the whole tree (routing to rmSync's recursive removal); Node deprecated the option here in favor of rmSync but still honors it.
differences: Options are the literal `{ recursive: true }` only; a missing path still throws (no `force`).

entries.name: fs.readdirSync(path[, { withFileTypes, recursive }])
entries.signature: readdirSync(path: string, options?: { withFileTypes?: true, recursive?: true }): string[] | Dirent[]
entries.description: Lists a directory's entries (excluding . and ..) as a string[], in whatever order the OS's own readdir() returns them — no ordering guarantee, matching real Node. Verified on both Darwin and x86-64 Linux via a compiled offsetof probe. With { withFileTypes: true } it returns Dirent[] — each with .name, .parentPath (the directory it was read from), and the full kind-predicate set .isFile()/.isDirectory()/.isSymbolicLink()/.isFIFO()/.isCharacterDevice()/.isBlockDevice()/.isSocket(), classified from the entry's d_type (from FindFirstFile attributes on Windows) without a per-file stat. With { recursive: true } it walks the whole subtree, returning every nested entry as a '/'-joined path relative to the start directory. Combining { recursive: true, withFileTypes: true } walks the subtree as Dirent[], each entry's .parentPath being the full path of its containing directory.

returns.desc: Directory entry names (recursive: relative paths), or Dirent objects when withFileTypes is set.

differences: `encoding: 'buffer'` is unsupported; recursive paths join with `'/'` (Node uses the platform separator).
A `DT_UNKNOWN` filesystem (rare) is not descended in recursive mode and reports all Dirent kinds `false` rather than falling back to `lstat`.

`Dirent` exposes `.name`/`.parentPath` and all seven kind predicates; the deprecated `.path` alias is intentionally not a member (current Node removed it in v24), so reading `dirent.path` is a compile-time error.

entries.name: fs.renameSync(oldPath, newPath)
entries.signature: renameSync(oldPath: string, newPath: string): void
entries.description: Renames/moves a file via POSIX rename(). Throws on failure.

entries.name: fs.copyFileSync(src, dest[, mode])
entries.signature: copyFileSync(src: string, dest: string, mode?: number): void
entries.description: Copies a file by composing the raw byte-count-aware read/write helpers — binary-safe, so a source file with an embedded null byte copies back whole. The optional mode bitmask honours COPYFILE_EXCL (bit 1): the copy fails with EEXIST if dest already exists (an atomic O_EXCL guard), instead of the default overwrite.
differences: `COPYFILE_FICLONE`/`FICLONE_FORCE` mode bits are accepted but a best-effort no-op (no reflink); `fs.constants.COPYFILE_EXCL`/`COPYFILE_FICLONE`/`COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE` name all three.

entries.name: Async variants (callback + fs.promises)
entries.statusRow: Async variants — callback (`fs.readFile(path, cb)`) + Promise (`fs.promises.readFile` / `import from 'fs/promises'`)
entries.signature: fs.readFile(path[, options], cb); await fs.promises.readFile(path[, options])
entries.description: Async forms of the sync set, with their options: readFile/writeFile/appendFile/unlink/mkdir/rmdir/rename/copyFile/readdir. readFile resolves to a Buffer, or a string with an encoding. The callback gets (err[, data]), data undefined on an error; the Promise rejects with the same Error the sync form throws. Each reuses its *Sync runtime helper verbatim, catching the throw via the compiler's setjmp catch primitive.
entries.snippet:
await fs.promises.writeFile('demo.txt', 'hi')
const text: string = await fs.promises.readFile('demo.txt', 'utf8')
differences: The async ops are genuinely non-blocking — they run on a background thread pool (default 4, UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE) and return a pending Promise the loop settles on completion (TDD-00185). An op given options beyond a utf8 encoding (a flag, a mode, recursive, withFileTypes, another readFile encoding) runs inline on the loop thread instead. The pool is POSIX-first; Windows keeps the inline path for now.
No async `stat`.

entries.name: fs.open / read / write / writev / fsync / close
entries.statusRow: fs.open / close / read / write / writev / fsync (callback form)
entries.signature: fs.open(path, flags?, mode?, cb); fs.read(fd, buffer, offset, length, position, cb); fs.write(fd, buffer | string, …, cb); fs.writev(fd, buffers, position?, cb); fs.fsync(fd, cb); fs.close(fd, cb?)
entries.description: The descriptor-level callback operations, with Node's argument forms (fs.read's options object and bare forms, fs.write's string form with a position and encoding), validation errors and system errors (code, errno, syscall, path). Each runs on the thread pool and calls back from the event loop.

returns.desc: The result arrives through the callback.

differences: On Windows a positioned read or write seeks, then transfers — not atomic against another operation on the same descriptor; not verified on Windows.

entries.name: fs.createReadStream / createWriteStream
entries.signature: fs.createReadStream(path, options?): fs.ReadStream; fs.createWriteStream(path, options?): fs.WriteStream
entries.description: A ReadStream is a Readable over the file: Buffer chunks (strings with an encoding), highWaterMark 64 KiB, start/end byte ranges. A WriteStream is a Writable: writes append in order, 'finish' then 'close'. Both open on the next tick ('open', 'ready'); a failed open or read is an 'error' event. Node's lib/internal/fs/streams.js, ported to TypeScript.
entries.snippet:
for await (const chunk of fs.createReadStream('demo.txt')) { /* Buffer */ }
fs.createReadStream('a.txt').pipe(fs.createWriteStream('b.txt'))
differences: The `fs` (custom operations) and `signal` options, and a `FileHandle` as `fd`, are not supported.

entries.name: fs.statSync(path) / fs.lstatSync(path)
entries.signature: statSync(path: string): Stats
entries.description: Reads file metadata into a Stats object. lstatSync does not follow a final symlink. The Stats value carries the full numeric surface — dev, mode, nlink, uid, gid, rdev, blksize, ino, size, blocks, atimeMs, mtimeMs, ctimeMs, birthtimeMs — plus the isFile()/isDirectory()/isSymbolicLink() predicates.

returns.desc: A Stats with the numeric metadata fields and isFile()/isDirectory()/isSymbolicLink().

differences: The Date-valued `atime`/`mtime`/`ctime`/`birthtime` accessors are not exposed — timestamps are integer-millisecond fields (`atimeMs` etc.) only.
`birthtimeMs` is 0 on Linux (glibc's struct stat has no creation time without statx); macOS reports the real value.

entries.name: fs.rmSync / realpathSync / mkdtempSync / symlinkSync / linkSync / readlinkSync / chmodSync / truncateSync / accessSync
entries.statusRow: fs.rmSync / realpathSync / mkdtempSync / symlinkSync / linkSync / readlinkSync / chmodSync / truncateSync / accessSync
entries.signature: rmSync(path: string, options?: { recursive: boolean, force: boolean }): void; linkSync(existingPath: string, newPath: string): void
entries.description: The rest of the sync path-management set: recursive removal, canonicalization, temp-directory creation, symlink create/read, hard links, permission bits, truncation, and existence/permission checks.
differences: `rmSync` options must be a `{ recursive, force }` boolean-literal object — no `maxRetries`/`retryDelay` (a Windows-centric retry knob).
`readlinkSync` reads targets of any length (a growing buffer); `accessSync`'s mode defaults to existence-only (`F_OK`) and `fs.constants.F_OK`/`R_OK`/`W_OK`/`X_OK` name the others.
`linkSync` makes a hard link (`CreateHardLinkW` on Windows — unprivileged, unlike `symlinkSync`); it takes no link-type argument.

entries.name: fs.openSync / closeSync / readSync / writeSync / fstatSync
entries.signature: openSync(path: string, flags: string): number
entries.description: The low-level file-descriptor API: open a path to an fd, read/write at the descriptor, stat it, and close it — for random-access or streaming patterns the whole-file helpers don't cover.

params.name: flags
params.desc: A string-literal mode: r r+ w w+ a a+ wx ax (or a raw numeric mask).

differences: `openSync` flags must be a string literal (`r r+ w w+ a a+ wx ax`) or a raw numeric mask — not a runtime-computed flag string. `fs.constants` exposes the access/copyFile constants and the `O_*` open flags (each resolved to the target OS's `<fcntl.h>` bits), so `openSync(p, fs.constants.O_WRONLY | fs.constants.O_CREAT)` works.
`writeSync` writes string data only (no Buffer/offset/length variant); `readSync`'s buffer must be a `Uint8Array`/`Buffer`.

entries.name: fs.fsyncSync / fdatasyncSync / ftruncateSync
entries.signature: fsyncSync(fd: number): void; ftruncateSync(fd: number, len?: number): void
entries.description: Durability and resize over an open file descriptor: flush buffered writes to disk (fsyncSync/fdatasyncSync) and resize the open file (ftruncateSync), completing the fd-based API alongside openSync/readSync/writeSync. On POSIX these are the fsync/ftruncate syscalls; on Windows they are Win32 shims (FlushFileBuffers / SetEndOfFile), so the same code runs on every host.

params.name: fd
params.desc: An open file descriptor from openSync.

params.name: len
params.desc: ftruncateSync only: the new file length; defaults to 0. Growing zero-fills.

returns.desc: Nothing; throws a coded Error on failure.

differences: `fdatasyncSync` is an alias for `fsyncSync` — the data-only optimization isn't observable in a file's contents.

A bad fd throws a coded `Error` (`e.code === 'EBADF'`); the message is `fd operation failed '': <reason>`, not Node's `EBADF: …, fsync` form. `err.syscall` (`'fsync'`/`'ftruncate'`/`'fstat'`) and the numeric `err.errno` match Node; only `err.path` is absent (fd ops carry no path in Node either).

entries.name: fs.fchmodSync(fd, mode)
entries.signature: fchmodSync(fd: number, mode: number): void
entries.description: chmodSync over an open file descriptor: fchmod(2) on POSIX; on Windows the same read-only-bit model as chmodSync, applied through the handle (FileBasicInfo, as libuv does). A socket or pipe fd is EBADF, and the thrown error is Node's fd-shaped `EBADF: bad file descriptor, fchmod`.

params.name: fd
params.desc: An open file descriptor from openSync.

returns.desc: Nothing; throws a coded Error on failure.

entries.name: fs.statfsSync(path)
entries.signature: statfsSync(path: string, options?: { bigint?: boolean }): { type, bsize, frsize, blocks, bfree, bavail, files, ffree }
entries.description: File-system statistics of the volume holding path: statfs(2) read against the platform's own struct on POSIX (Darwin's frsize is bsize, as libuv reports); on Windows GetDiskFreeSpaceW of the path's volume, with type/files/ffree 0 as in Node. The path itself is probed first, so a missing file is `ENOENT: no such file or directory, statfs '<path>'`.

returns.desc: { type, bsize, frsize, blocks, bfree, bavail, files, ffree }, all numbers.

entries.snippet:
const s = fs.statfsSync(os.tmpdir())
console.log(s.bavail * s.bsize) // free bytes available to this user
differences: The `{ bigint: true }` option is accepted and ignored — the fields are always numbers.

entries.name: fs.utimesSync(path, …) / fs.futimesSync(fd, …)
entries.signature: utimesSync(path: string, atime: number | Date, mtime: number | Date): void; futimesSync(fd: number, atime: number | Date, mtime: number | Date): void
entries.description: Sets a file's access and modification times, by path (utimesSync) or open fd (futimesSync). atime/mtime are seconds (Node's number form) or a Date (its epoch); sub-second precision is carried as microseconds. On POSIX these are utimes(2)/futimes(2); on Windows a SetFileTime shim converting Unix time to the 1601-epoch FILETIME (keyed on the path or _get_osfhandle(fd)).

params.name: atime
params.desc: New access time — seconds since the epoch, or a Date.

params.name: mtime
params.desc: New modification time — seconds since the epoch, or a Date.

returns.desc: Nothing; throws a coded Error on failure.

differences: `atime`/`mtime` accept a number or `Date` only — a numeric string (which Node also coerces) is not supported.

A missing path throws a coded `Error` (`e.code === 'ENOENT'`) that also carries `err.syscall` (the bare syscall — `'open'`/`'stat'`/`'scandir'`/…), `err.path`, and the numeric `err.errno` (libuv's value, as in Node: the negated errno on POSIX — `-2` for ENOENT — and libuv's own numbering on Windows, `-4058`); only the message text differs from Node's `ENOENT: …, <syscall> '<path>'` format.

entries.name: fs.watch
entries.signature: fs.watch(path, listener?): FSWatcher; watcher.on('change'|'rename', (evt, name) => …); watcher.close()
entries.description: Native, event-driven file-change watching folded into the event loop — no stat-polling. Returns an FSWatcher that fires (eventType, filename) on each change; .close() stops watching and lets a watch-only program exit. Backends: Linux inotify, macOS kqueue/EVFILT_VNODE, Windows ReadDirectoryChangesW.
entries.snippet: const w = fs.watch('file.txt', (evt, name) => { console.log(evt); w.close() })
differences: `filename` names the changed entry on Linux, but is the **watched path** on macOS (kqueue watches an fd, not directory entries — Node uses FSEvents there); a documented divergence, the file-watch case is faithful.
One listener slot per event (`.on(...)`, arrow-literal only) — the Worker/ChildProcess posture, not the full EventEmitter.
`recursive` is honoured natively on macOS/Windows; on Linux (inotify) it watches only the named path. `encoding` accepts only `'utf8'`; no coalescing/ordering guarantees (as in Node).

entries.name: File / FileReader / FileSystemFileHandle
entries.signature: // not supported
entries.description: The browser-flavored File API is not planned — these model browser sandbox/permission concepts this compiler has no equivalent for. A native CLI/microservice program has direct filesystem access via the fs functions above instead.
